# Insurance proposal software: 16 questions brokers ask, answered


Abhi Balijepalli


Co-founder, CopyCat


Published November 23, 2026


·


11 min read


The short version


- Proposal software should turn carrier quote PDFs into an editable, agency-branded proposal, with every premium, limit and deductible linked to its source page.
- It should compare several carriers in one proposal, show what changed at renewal, and explain coverage in words a client understands.
- Every producer should work from the same template, with version history and a shared view of who did what.
- CopyCat Basics is $99 a month after a 7-day free trial. Agency teams use CopyCat Pro, quoted after a demo.


These are the questions independent agencies ask when they shop for insurance proposal software, grouped by the part of the job they cover. Each answer says what good looks like and how CopyCat does it. For a vendor-by-vendor shortlist, see our[guide to choosing insurance proposal software](https://www.runcopycat.com/best-insurance-proposal-software) .


We make CopyCat. Test any answer here on one of your own accounts before you take our word for it.


## From carrier quotes to a proposal


### 1. What software do agencies use to create client-facing proposals?


Approach How it works Tradeoff


Word or PowerPoint templates Values copied from each quote by hand Free, but slow, and every producer’s version drifts


AMS proposal builders Built from policy data in the agency management system, such as Vertafore Proposal Builder in AMS360 Only as good as the system’s data, and new-business quotes are often not in it yet


Interactive web proposals A hosted page or video for the client Good for presentation; check how the quote details get in


AI proposal software Reads the carrier quote PDFs and builds the proposal on your template Check accuracy, source links and editing


CopyCat is[AI proposal software](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-software) for P&C agencies, commercial and personal lines.


### 2. Can proposal software create an editable proposal straight from carrier quote PDFs?


Yes. Drop in the carrier quotes along with schedules, statements of values and finance agreements, and CopyCat builds the proposal on your agency’s template. It opens in CopyCat’s built-in document editor, so you click in and type, or ask the AI to make a change, without exporting to Word. When it is ready, export the client PDF.


### 3. Which proposal tools link premiums and coverage back to the source quote page?


Look for a source link on every number a client will rely on: premium, limits, deductibles, taxes and fees. In CopyCat each extracted value carries a citation to the carrier page it came from, so an account manager checks a limit with one click before the proposal goes out. That review is also your record if a client later asks where a number came from.


### 4. Can one proposal compare limits, deductibles and exclusions across several carriers?


It should, because that comparison is what the client is paying you for. CopyCat lays competing carrier options side by side by line of business, with limits, deductibles, premiums and exclusions, each cited. For a deeper side-by-side,[Coverage Comparison](https://www.runcopycat.com/coverage-comparison) builds a cited quote or renewal comparison with a one-page client summary, with no cap on the number of documents, and turns it into a proposal when you are ready.


### 5. Does it handle commercial and personal lines in one workflow?


CopyCat does both in one workspace.[Commercial proposals](https://www.runcopycat.com/commercial-insurance-proposal-software) handle multi-line and specialty accounts: general liability, property, auto, workers comp, umbrella, inland marine, cyber and more.[Personal lines proposals](https://www.runcopycat.com/personal-lines-proposal-software) build from homeowners, auto, umbrella and other household quotes, with payment plans laid out for the client.


## Renewals and client clarity


### 6. Can it build renewal proposals that show premium and coverage changes?


A renewal proposal should put the expiring terms next to the renewal so the client sees what moved, not just the new premium. Add the expiring policy with the renewal quotes and CopyCat shows the expiring terms beside the renewal options. For a line-by-line view of coverage changes,[a renewal comparison](https://www.runcopycat.com/commercial-renewal-comparison-software) lays out every change with its source page and hands it to the proposal.


### 7. How do proposals explain premiums and coverage so clients understand them?


Plain-language coverage descriptions next to the numbers, a clear recommendation, and a short version for the client who won’t read twenty pages. CopyCat produces the full proposal, a one-page summary and an email summary from the same account. Proposals can be produced in English, Spanish or French, with limits and premiums kept exactly as quoted.


### 8. Can a proposal be tailored to a client’s risk priorities?


The template should be consistent; the advice should not be. In CopyCat the producer writes or edits the recommendation for each client, or asks the[AI editor](https://www.runcopycat.com/blog/agentic-ai-insurance-proposal-editor) for a change such as “lead with the cyber exposure” or “explain why we recommend the higher umbrella limit.” The AI makes the edit in the document, and the producer reviews it before it goes out.


## Brand and team


### 9. How do agencies keep proposals consistent across producers?


Put the brand in the template, not in each producer’s habits. In CopyCat the agency’s template carries the logo, colors, sections and standard language, and every producer and account manager builds on it, so a proposal looks the same whoever made it. A shared board shows every proposal with its owner, and an analytics dashboard shows volume across the team.


### 10. Can brokers edit AI-generated proposal copy and layout before delivery?


They have to be able to. In CopyCat you click into any section and type, reorder sections, move columns, or describe the change and let the agentic editor carry it out. Nothing reaches a client until a person exports it.


### 11. Do proposal platforms support team review and version history?


CopyCat keeps a version history on every proposal, so a reviewer can see earlier versions and restore one, and an activity log records who created, edited and exported each proposal. Proposals sit on a shared team board with owners, so a manager can pick up any account.


### 12. How do we move our branded template when we switch platforms?


Send your current proposal as a PDF. On CopyCat Pro, the CopyCat team rebuilds it as your agency template and runs a branding call with you before rollout, so the format your clients know carries over and the final say stays with you. That also covers agencies without an in-house design team: the template is designed for you. On Basics, pick a standard template and add your logo and colors. See[proposal templates](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-template) .


## Buying


### 13. How much does insurance proposal software cost for a small agency?


CopyCat Basics is $99 a month for a solo agency, with 100 credits a month and a 7-day free trial. Agencies with two or more people, or higher volume, use CopyCat Pro, quoted on team size and usage after a demo. There is no setup fee and monthly plans cancel anytime. See[pricing](https://www.runcopycat.com/pricing) .


### 14. Can we try it before buying? Are there free tools?


Word and PowerPoint templates are free, but every proposal is retyped. CopyCat Basics starts with a 7-day free trial; a card starts the trial and is not charged until it ends. Agency teams can bring one of their own accounts to a demo and watch the proposal build from their quotes.


### 15. Does it sync with our agency management system?


CopyCat Pro connects to HawkSoft and AMS360. Pick the client and CopyCat imports the in-force policies into the proposal or renewal comparison, then files the finished PDF back on the client. On any other system, upload the quotes and policies directly. CopyCat works beside your AMS; it doesn’t replace it. More in[AI tools that integrate with HawkSoft](https://www.runcopycat.com/blog/ai-tools-that-integrate-with-hawksoft) .


### 16. What onboarding and support should we expect?


Ask who sets up the template, who trains the team and how fast support answers. CopyCat Pro includes guided onboarding with a branding call, training calls with our team and support with average response times under 15 minutes. Basics includes email support.
